newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangxi Copper seen raising fund to reduce debt.
newsitem.headline: Jiangxi Copper seen raising fund to reduce debt.

text.p: China copper-producer Jiangxi Copper Co Ltd is expected to use US$200 million in flotation proceeds to repay short-term debt and expand production facilities, analysts said on Monday.

"The company will use about 1.2 billion yuan, the majority of the proceeds, to repay certain of its short-term indebtedness and the balance will be used to expand its copper production," said an analyst after attending a company presentation on Monday.
Analysts said the company had revealed short-term debt -- to be repaid within one year -- of about HK$2 billion and long-term debt of about HK$1.675 billion.

Jiangxi Copper is expected to issue 628.212 million H-shares in a global offering at prices ranging from HK$2.13 to HK$2.72 a share, representing a price to earnings multiple of 11 to 14 times, analysts said.
Analysts said 10 percent of the issue was expected to be offered to Hong Kong investors through a public offering and 90 percent was earmarked for international placement elsewhere.
But if the Hong Kong portion of the offering is more than 15 times subscribed, another 15 percent will be reallocated to the Hong Kong tranche from the international portion, analysts said
They expected Jiangxi Copper to hold a roadshow in Europe from May 27 to 29, and from May 30 to June 5 in the United States.
The public offering in Hong Kong is expected to run from June 2 to 5, and the issue price is expected to be fixed on June 5, analysts said.
Dealing in the company's shares is expected to begin on June 12, they added.
Merrill Lynch is expected to be the global coordinator and sponsor of the issue, they said.
Jiangxi Copper is engaged in copper mining, milling, smelting and refining facilities in northeastern Jiangxi province in China.
It produced 116,547 tonnes of copper cathode in 1996, and sales of the copper cathode accounted for about 72.1 percent of the company's total revenues of 2.996 billion yuan in 1996.
"It forecast a profit to be not less than 500 million yuan for the year ending in 1997," one analyst said.
Jiangxi Copper posted a profit of 211.8 million yuan for the year ended in December 1996, compared with 417 million yuan in 1995 and 192.5 million yuan in 1994, analysts said.
Turnover was 2.996 billion yuan in 1996, 3.12 billion yuan in 1995 and 2.23 billion yuan in 1994, they added.
